steps.name: Library size and count distribution QC
caveats: Library size alone cannot distinguish technical shallow sequencing from a biologically atypical sample; downstream PCA/clustering in T1S2 and T1S3 are needed to triangulate
steps.question: What are the raw library sizes (total counts) for all 12 samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control), and how does sample_01 compare to the cohort median/IQR and to its condition group?
constraints: Use the raw integer counts.csv and metadata.csv exactly as provided (12000 x 13 counts matrix, 12 x 2 metadata)
Do not filter or drop sample_01 at this stage — this is descriptive QC only
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample total raw counts computed from counts.csv for all 12 samples
Library sizes reported as a table and a bar plot, samples ordered/colored by condition
Median, IQR, and fold-deviation of sample_01 from the cohort median explicitly stated
Non-zero gene count / detection rate per sample also reported as a secondary QC metric

steps.name: Normalization and PCA of all 12 samples
caveats: A very low library size can inflate variance-stabilized values for that sample and pull it out on a PC that reflects technical depth rather than biology — call this out explicitly if seen
steps.question: After variance-stabilizing normalization, how do the 12 samples separate on PCA (PC1/PC2, colored by AD-lesional vs control), and where does sample_01 fall relative to its condition group and relative to the other 11 samples?
constraints: Compute DESeq2 size factors / vst on the full 12-sample count matrix, not on a subset
Report PCA both with and without sample_01 if its low library size visibly distorts size-factor estimation or PC loadings, so the effect of the shallow sample on the projection is transparent
acceptance_criteria: Raw counts normalized with DESeq2 vst or rlog (or an equivalent size-factor-aware transform) prior to PCA
PCA computed on the normalized matrix (e.g. top variable genes), PC1 and PC2 percent variance explained reported
PCA scatter plot produced with points labeled by sample ID and colored by condition (lesional vs control)
Explicit statement of whether sample_01 is a PCA outlier (e.g. distance from group centroid / from all other samples) and whether it still separates by condition along PC1 or PC2

steps.name: Sample-to-sample distance matrix and hierarchical clustering
caveats: Euclidean distance on vst-normalized data can still be sensitive to a very low-depth sample's added technical noise; note this when interpreting sample_01's position
steps.question: Based on pairwise sample-to-sample distances computed from the normalized expression data, does sample_01 cluster with its assigned condition group (lesional or control) or does it fall out as an outlier distinct from all other samples?
constraints: Use the same normalized matrix produced in T1S2 for consistency between the PCA and the distance-matrix views
acceptance_criteria: Pairwise sample-to-sample distance matrix computed (e.g. Euclidean distance on vst/rlog-normalized data, or Poisson distance which is robust to differing library depth)
Distance matrix rendered as an annotated heatmap with hierarchical clustering dendrogram, samples labeled with condition
Explicit report of which cluster/branch sample_01 falls into and its mean distance to same-condition vs opposite-condition samples
Any secondary outlier samples besides sample_01 are also flagged if present

steps.name: Synthesized QC verdict on sample_01 and cohort
caveats: A definitive technical-vs-biological determination for sample_01 would ideally involve external QC metrics (e.g. RIN, mapping rate) not present in this data profile; the verdict here is necessarily based only on count-derived evidence
steps.question: Combining library size, PCA position, and sample-to-sample distance evidence, what is the verdict on sample_01 (retain as-is, retain with caveat, or exclude from downstream differential expression) and is the remaining 11/12-sample cohort otherwise clean for testing?
constraints: Do not run or imply any differential expression test in this step — this plan is QC-only per the research question
acceptance_criteria: Verdict explicitly integrates the three lines of evidence from T1S1-T1S3 (library size deviation, PCA position, clustering behavior)

Verdict states a concrete recommendation for the downstream DE analysis (e.g. keep and rely on size-factor normalization vs flag as a sensitivity-analysis exclusion) with the reasoning made explicit rather than asserted
Report notes whether any sample besides sample_01 shows a comparable anomaly
No differential expression or hypothesis testing is performed in this step — QC synthesis only, consistent with the research question asking to look at samples 'before we test anything'

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq QC: library size, PCA, sample distances
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a pre-testing QC pass on a 12-sample (6 lesional AD vs 6 control), single-batch, unpaired bulk RNA-seq skin dataset with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples; the counts.csv has 13 columns including the gene symbol column). The data profile flags sample_01 as having a library size ~4x below the median, which is the central question to resolve before any differential expression is run. The plan is a single coherent QC track: (1) compute and report per-sample library sizes (total counts) and flag outliers against the group median/IQR, (2) apply a standard variance-stabilizing normalization (DESeq2 rlog/vst or equivalent) and run PCA colored by condition to see whether sample_01 and any other sample separate from their group, (3) compute a sample-to-sample distance matrix/heatmap (Euclidean on normalized data or Poisson distance suited to count outliers) with hierarchical clustering to see if sample_01 clusters with its condition group or is an outlier, and (4) synthesize the three lines of evidence into an explicit verdict on sample_01 — retain, downweight, or exclude — with the reasoning stated. All steps operate on the same raw counts + metadata files already profiled; no external data or reference sets are needed for this QC-only task.
